gloss: to leave in writing; to write down for posterity

definitions.gloss: to leave in writing; to write down for posterity; to record
definitions.explanation: To write something so that it remains as a record after one is gone or for future reference.

examples.japanese: {日記|にっき}に{書|か}き{残|のこ}した。
examples.english: I left it written in my diary.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}が{書|か}き{残|のこ}した{手紙|てがみ}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: A letter that my grandfather left behind was found.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はその{体験|たいけん}を{後世|こうせい}のために{書|か}き{残|のこ}そうと{決心|けっしん}した。
examples.english: He decided to write down his experiences for future generations.

notes:
A compound verb combining {書|か}く (to write) and {残|のこ}す (to leave behind). It emphasizes that the writing survives or endures, often implying the author has since passed away or that the record is meant for posterity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記録|きろく}を{書|か}き{残|のこ}す: to leave a written record
- {遺言|ゆいごん}を{書|か}き{残|のこ}す: to leave a will in writing
- {後世|こうせい}に{書|か}き{残|のこ}す: to write down for posterity

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {記|しる}す: to write down; to record — more literary, focuses on the act of recording
- {残|のこ}す: to leave behind — broader, not limited to writing
- {書|か}き{留|と}める: to jot down; to note — focuses on capturing information in the moment
